identity.archival_project: 東吳大學城區部行政資料處理中心新建工程
identity.identity_evidence: Museum six-sheet common project/architect catalogue and title blocks, T-shaped floor plans and distinctive elevation correspondence; locally saved photographer article explicitly connects the second building/Chuqiu alias and Wang Da-Hong. Official planning page was not obtained and is not claimed as evidence.

decision.adequacy: The six large as-built sheets provide B1–7F plans, RF, two sections, four different elevations and roof-room details. Combined with the two completed photographs, they close the principal T-shaped exterior and roof junctions sufficiently for a source-limited whole-building model. I found no unresolved major mass/roof junction requiring another photograph before a builder can be assigned.
decision.not_required: An aerial or separate photograph of every elevation is not automatically required when the adopted archival as-built drawings actually describe those surfaces.
decision.remaining_limit: North long face, west short face and much of RF are drawing-derived, not photographed in the present collection. Their present-day equipment/fenestration is not verified.
decision.version: Archival as-built exterior geometry, cross-checked and locally informed by author-reported 2025 visible east/south exteriors; neither a wholly photographed 2025 roof nor a precise 2026 survey.

visual_findings.finding: Continuous flat T-shaped roof/parapet, three non-identical staircase/plantroom groups and explicit roofs/elevations for them. The right/east cross-wing joins the long bar at common floor levels. Upper roof geometry is not a generic single cuboid.

Two northern long rectangular objects are labeled rooftop water tanks, not openings or skylights. Original-pixel inspection reads H=149 and 980×160; the builder must cross-read the centimetre units and dimensions before modelling. Three circles near the central group denote cooling equipment positions/loads, not circular skylights; current equipment arrangement is unverified.

Original-pixel section reads GL-to-roof 2400 cm, GL-to-1FL 90 cm, 1F-to-2F 345 cm, the five 2F-to-7F intervals 323 cm each, and 7F-to-roof 350 cm (90+345+5×323+350=2400). These are drawing readings rather than an independent site measurement; do not distribute seven equal floors or expose all B1 above grade.

All four faces have distinct wide/narrow bay patterns and entry locations. The triangular lines above the roof are lightning-rod protection diagrams, not pitched roofs. A flat roof is independently controlled by RF and section.

True full floor plans preserve the T footprint and its unequal core/entry organisation. Seventh-level perimeter slightly wraps/extends relative to lower levels; no blanket major top-floor setback is justified. Interior stairs should not automatically be made exterior stair towers.

Photo07 is the Taoyuan Street east short-end entrance of the T-wing, corresponding to the east elevation central entry and flanking narrow windows. It is not the opposing long face. Visible canopy beams, supporting columns, glass-block upper door zone and entry steps must not be replaced with the separately drawn north entrance three-double-door detail.

Photo12 shows the south court-facing long side and the projecting southern end of the eastern T-wing. Upper narrow vertical slots, concrete frames, masonry fields and visible roof groups correspond. The closer cross-wing appears higher by perspective; this is not evidence for an extra storey.

Visible material families can support approximate concrete, brick and low-saturation glazing display proxies; shadows are not evidence for black walls. Tree-obscured and unphotographed details remain drawing-derived or explicitly simplified. Adjacent sixth-building clock tower and first building are excluded.

required_builder_conditions: Independently register plan north/east axes and both photographs before creating geometry; preserve T-wing handedness and each separate elevation rather than mirror-copying.
Use explicit printed dimensions with cross-checks and uneven section levels. Do not convert scan pixels using paper 1:200 as if digital DPI were surveyed scale.

Represent the complete main T mass, flat RF/parapet, the three unequal roof-room groups and the two archival low water-tank masses. No triangular lightning-envelope roofs, false skylights, extra storey or invented connector.
Keep the source version explicit: unphotographed north/west/RF geometry derives from archival as-built documents. Do not call all equipment or the whole roof verified as 2025/2026 current state.
Apply photo07 to the east entrance only. Preserve visible canopy/column supports and underside shape; the north three-door entrance drawing is a different facade.
Treat B1 as underground except documented exposed threshold/base relationships. A display base is a declared modelling aid, not evidence for a surrounding campus wedge.

Tiny plant equipment/rods, fine mullions and lettering may be omitted or thickened only with an explicit source-versus-manufacturing approximation statement. Do not manufacture unsupported geometry to fill unseen areas.

Keep all original source scans and photographs private. Public outputs may carry factual source references/attribution; no source-image textures or redistributed source scans in the model ZIP. Museum record labels CC BY-NC; this review is not a copyright/licensing determination.

After parent assignment, a separate builder must produce new geometry/format/native edit-reopen/rebuild/raw topology/thickness/support QA and five exact core previews, with independent review and actual ZIP/source-extraction closure. No manufacturing approval is inherited from another model, and no physical print is claimed.
